# Glossary {#sec-glossary}

Plain-language definitions of the terms this book uses.

**Account (Slurm)**
: The *project* that a job is charged to (e.g. `cowy-firesurro`). Required on every job via
  `--account`. Not your username. See @sec-anatomy.

**ARCC**
: Advanced Research Computing Center — the UW group that runs MedicineBow.

**ASCEND / ARID**
: The NSF Regional Innovation Engine (ASCEND) and its wildfire-resilience program (ARID) that
  many readers of this book work under. See the preface.

**Backfill**
: Slurm slotting a small, short job into a gap in the schedule without delaying higher-priority
  jobs. Why short jobs start fast. See @sec-priority.

**Batch job**
: A job submitted as a script with `sbatch` that runs unattended when scheduled. The normal way
  to run work. See @sec-anatomy.

**Checkpoint**
: A periodic save of a job's state so it can *resume* instead of *restart* after a preemption,
  timeout, or crash. Essential for long jobs. See @sec-checkpointing.

**Compute node**
: A machine where computation actually runs, allocated to you by Slurm. Distinct from a login
  node. See @sec-cluster.

**Condo model**
: The funding model where research groups buy nodes (`inv-*`) and others borrow them when idle,
  subject to reclaim/preemption. See @sec-preemption.

**Core-hour**
: One CPU core used for one hour — the unit your allocation is measured in. Reserving 8 cores
  for 1 hour costs 8 core-hours whether or not you use them.

**`DenyOnLimit`**
: A QOS flag meaning an over-limit request is **rejected at submit time**, not silently queued.
  See @sec-partitions.

**Fair-share**
: A priority factor reflecting your account's recent usage relative to its share; heavy recent
  use temporarily lowers your priority. See @sec-priority.

**GRES (Generic RESource)**
: How you request GPUs: `--gres=gpu:1` or `--gres=gpu:h100:2`. See @sec-gpu.

**Investor / `inv-*`**
: Nodes/partitions owned by a specific group, who get top priority; others can be preempted off
  them. See @sec-preemption.

**Job array**
: One script run many times with a varying index (`$SLURM_ARRAY_TASK_ID`), for parameter sweeps
  and ensembles. Max 10,000 tasks. See @sec-arrays.

**Lmod / module**
: The system that loads specific software versions into your shell on demand. Hierarchical:
  many modules are hidden until you load a compiler. Use `module spider`. See @sec-modules.

**Login node**
: The shared front-end machine (`mblog1`, `mblog2`) you land on when you connect. For editing
  and submitting — **not** for computing. See @sec-cluster.

**MedicineBow**
: UW/ARCC's current flagship HPC cluster. The subject of this book.

**MPI**
: Message Passing Interface — the standard for a single parallel program spanning many cores or
  nodes that communicate. Launched with `srun`. Contrast with job arrays. See @sec-ladder.

**OnDemand (Open OnDemand)**
: The web portal at `medicinebow.arcc.uwyo.edu` — file browser, terminal, and interactive apps.
  See @sec-first-login.

**OOM (Out Of Memory)**
: When a job exceeds its memory reservation and is killed. Fix by raising `--mem`. See @sec-fail.

**Partition**
: A named pool of nodes with particular hardware (`mb`, `mb-h100`, `teton`, `non-investor`, …).
  Chosen with `--partition`. See @sec-partitions.

**Preemption**
: An investor reclaiming a borrowed node, causing your job to be killed and (here) requeued.
  See @sec-preemption.

**Priority**
: The score that orders pending jobs. On MedicineBow it's dominated by QOS (weight 200). See
  @sec-priority.

**QOS (Quality of Service)**
: The service tier that sets your max walltime, resource cap, and priority (`debug`, `fast`,
  `normal`, `long`, …). See @sec-partitions.

**Requeue**
: Putting a killed (preempted/failed) job back in the pending queue to start over. Pair with
  checkpointing. See @sec-preemption.

**Scratch (`/gscratch`, `$SCRATCH`)**
: Fast, large, temporary storage purged after 90 days of inactivity. Not backed up. See
  @sec-storage.

**`seff`**
: A command showing a finished job's CPU and memory efficiency — use it to right-size. See
  @sec-monitoring.

**Slurm**
: The scheduler that manages all jobs on the cluster. See @sec-why-scheduler.

**Snapshot**
: A point-in-time copy of a filesystem, on the *same array* as the live data. Protects against
  accidental deletion, **not** hardware loss. Not a backup. See @sec-storage.

**Walltime**
: Real elapsed clock time a job is allowed (`--time`). The job is killed at the limit. See
  @sec-resources.
